tagline: From the Pemigewasset over to the Connecticut by way of Moosilauke.
intro: From Lincoln the route runs south through Campton and crosses the Pemigewasset into Plymouth, the college town where Nathaniel Hawthorne died on a holiday in 1864. NH 25 then follows the Baker River up through Rumney and Wentworth to Warren, with Mount Moosilauke in view, and NH 25C crosses over to Piermont on the Connecticut. The last miles run north on Route 10 to Haverhill Corner and North Haverhill.

The official loop runs 120 miles from North Woodstock, and this map follows about 62 of them, Lincoln to North Haverhill. The rest goes north to Woodsville and home by Bath and Kinsman Notch, over three of the oldest and longest covered bridges in the state.

moments.title: Plymouth
moments.text: Daniel Webster lost his first criminal case at the old courthouse in 1806, and the building now houses the historical society.

moments.title: Warren
moments.text: A Redstone missile has stood on the village green since 1971, brought up from Alabama in honor of Senator Norris Cotton, a Warren native.

moments.title: Haverhill Corner
moments.text: Federal houses and the 1827 Congregational church stand around a pair of grassy commons on Route 10, a county seat left behind when the railroad went to Woodsville.
